speaker: Unknown
en: Well, hi, folks.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, thank you for joining me.
zh: 所以，是的，谢谢大家的到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name's Remy.
zh: 我叫 Remy。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am on the Strategic Projects team at TailScale.
zh: 我在 TailScale 的战略项目团队工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And more specifically, I actually work on our AI Gateway, Aperture.
zh: 更具体地说，我实际负责的是我们的 AI Gateway——Aperture。

speaker: Unknown
en: And today I want to talk a little bit about what it means or what it's going to take to have an AI future without the lock-in.
zh: 今天我想稍微谈一谈，拥有一个没有锁定的 AI 未来意味着什么，或者需要付出什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of the lock-in that we've seen over the last 12 months.
zh: 我想谈谈我们在过去 12 个月里看到的很多锁定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, so if we take a look real quick at the last 12 months, I think it can really be described quite a bit by the phrase token maxing.
zh: 是的，如果我们快速回顾一下过去 12 个月，我认为它很大程度上可以用一个词来描述，就是 token maxing。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean that in the kind of negative sense that you might kind of hear outside of the kind of AI enthusiast circle.
zh: 我说的是一种负面意义上的意思，就像你在 AI 爱好者圈子之外可能会听到的那种。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean that in the sort of, you know, it's been a year of trying to figure out, you know, what we can do with million token context windows, with the ability to get context from anywhere, right?
zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这一年大家一直在试图弄清楚，我们用百万 token 的上下文窗口、用从任何地方获取上下文的能力能做什么，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not just, you know, MCP being everywhere, but, you know,
zh: 不仅仅是，你知道，MCP 无处不在，而是，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: Also having coding tools that are great at finding context, using the CLI, bringing that context into the model, bringing it into everything that you need, and going from there.
zh: 还有那些擅长寻找上下文的编码工具，使用 CLI，把上下文带进模型，把它带进你需要的一切东西里，然后从那里继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been pretty cool.
zh: 这挺酷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really made truly agentic coding possible, having all of this.
zh: 它真正让真正的智能体编码成为可能，拥有这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, it's quite cool.
zh: 所以，是的，相当酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're going to see not just agentic coding, but other agentic use cases continue to take off as we
zh: 而且我们会看到，不仅仅是智能体编码，还有其他智能体用例会继续起飞，随着我们

speaker: Unknown
en: as we do this.
zh: 这样做下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Token maxing is cool, but it has problems.
zh: Token maxing 很酷，但它有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's obvious problems.
zh: 有明显的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very expensive.
zh: 它非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an extremely expensive endeavor.
zh: 这是一项极其昂贵的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the last 12 months are
zh: 我想过去 12 个月是

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, have maybe been marked by, hey, we have, you know, unlimited AI budget.
zh: 你知道，也许是以「嘿，我们有，你知道，无限的 AI 预算」为标志的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's changed here in the last few months in terms of, you know, what it means to, you know, what it means to use AI.
zh: 而这在过去几个月里已经发生了变化，就，你知道，使用 AI 意味着什么而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also, I mean, you know, it's expensive, like just generally, if you're doing it, you're right.
zh: 它也是，我是说，你知道，它很贵，就像一般来说，如果你在做这件事，你是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it also, it does incentivize what I would call like wasted tokens by default.
zh: 但它也确实激励了我所说的默认浪费 token 的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I work on an AI gateway.
zh: 我是说，我做的是一个 AI 网关。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use our AI gateway.
zh: 我们使用我们自己的 AI 网关。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get to see all of the usage from the AI gateway.
zh: 我能看到来自这个 AI 网关的所有使用情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would not believe the number of sessions that are hundreds or thousands of messages long where nobody clears the context.
zh: 你不会相信有多少会话长达数百甚至数千条消息，而没有人清除上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just kind of keep going.
zh: 它们就那么一直继续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's helpful sometimes, but it's pretty surprising.
zh: 我是说，这有时候是有帮助的，但这挺令人惊讶的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will have tens of millions of tokens of a session where the cache is basically maxed out the entire time.
zh: 你会看到单个会话有数千万的 token，其中缓存基本上整个时间都被打满了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gets really expensive.
zh: 这变得非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other thing is, right, so, you know, this has been an exciting time, right?
zh: 另一件事是，对吧，所以，你知道，这是一段激动人心的时期，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: People are doing new things, building new things, but this has led to, you know, in many cases, very vertically integrated tool chains.
zh: 人们在尝试新事物，构建新东西，但这导致，你知道，在很多情况下，非常垂直整合的工具链。

speaker: Unknown
en: Claude Code is obviously, you know, a big one, Codex, right?
zh: Claude Code 显然，你知道，是个大块头，还有 Codex，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody's kind of building up their, you know, for all the way from the model, you know, all the way out of the top, you know, building their
zh: 每个人都在构建他们自己的，你知道，从模型一路到最顶层，你知道，构建他们的

speaker: Unknown
en: Building their agents, building their toolchains.
zh: 构建他们的智能体，构建他们的工具链。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of problems there.
zh: 那里有很多问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: My question in terms of this is, how do we address these problems?
zh: 我对此的问题是，我们如何解决这些问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: In particular, how do we address the lock-in and how do we actually improve how we use AI such that we can use it for things that aren't just essentially frontier tasks or where we're just wasting money, wasting tokens?
zh: 特别是，我们如何解决锁定问题，以及我们如何真正改进我们使用 AI 的方式，使得我们可以把它用于那些不只是一线的、前沿的任务，或者不再是我们只是在浪费钱、浪费 token 的场景？

speaker: Unknown
en: That sort of thing.
zh: 诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But first, I want to talk about how not to address the problem.
zh: 但首先，我想谈谈如何不去解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a super, super common thing.
zh: 而这是一个非常非常常见的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So over the last six months, we've been talking to, I've literally been talking to hundreds and hundreds of folks about their AI spend, their AI usage, right?
zh: 所以在过去六个月里，我们一直在和——我真的在和成百上千的人谈论他们的 AI 支出、他们的 AI 使用情况，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the kind of benefit of working on an AI gateway.
zh: 这就是在 AI 网关上工作的好处之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Folks come to you, they're like, I don't know what's going on.
zh: 人们会来找你，说：我不知道发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know we're using a lot of AI.
zh: 我知道我们用了大量的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get, you know, I get an Anthropic bill every day.
zh: 你知道，我每天都会收到 Anthropic 的账单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get a Codex bill every day.
zh: 我每天都会收到 Codex 的账单。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, it's not just that.
zh: 所以，你知道，不只是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I see it all the time.
zh: 你知道，我一直都能看到这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, what do I do?
zh: 那么，你知道，我该怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: They usually come with one kind of solution in mind, and that is, oh, we're just gonna, like,
zh: 他们通常带着一种已经想好的解决方案来，那就是，哦，我们打算就这样，

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody seems to be using Claude Code right now.
zh: 现在似乎每个人都在用 Claude Code。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're just going to consolidate on a single vendor.
zh: 所以我们就统一到单一供应商上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe two vendors.
zh: 也许两家供应商。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe two vendors.
zh: 也许两家供应商。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're like, I need to get a handle on this.
zh: 所以他们说，我需要掌控住这个局面。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I get a handle on this?
zh: 我怎么才能掌控住这个局面？

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, yeah, I will say everybody's going to use this.
zh: 好，是的，我会说大家都用这个吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just going to use this thing.
zh: 我们就用这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not a great idea.
zh: 这不是一个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might seem obvious sitting here that this may be not a great idea, but when you're in that panic zone of we've spent a lot of money and we don't know how exactly, and finance is talking to you, IT is being like, what are you doing?
zh: 坐在这里看，这可能不是个好主意似乎显而易见，但当你处在那种恐慌区——我们花了很多钱但不知道具体花在哪，财务在找你谈话，IT 在质问你：你在干什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We said to use AI, but maybe not use that much AI.
zh: 我们说过要用 AI，但也许不该用那么多 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a pretty natural response to go, OK, I'm going to consolidate everything down.
zh: 这时候一个很自然的反应就是：好，我要把所有东西整合收敛。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, I'm going to have control of this.
zh: 好，我要掌控住这个局面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, I think this is kind of peeking at what we're going to see the next 12 months and what people are actually trying to do, at least at the, you know, kind of frontier is what I would like to call ROI maxing, right?
zh: 而且，你知道，我觉得这在某种程度上预示了未来 12 个月我们会看到的情况，以及人们真正在尝试做的事情——至少在我愿意称之为 ROI 最大化（ROI maxing）的前沿上，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not going to be token maxing.
zh: 我们不再做 token 最大化（token maxing）了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be ROI maxing.
zh: 我们要做 ROI 最大化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's really just a necessity, right?
zh: 你知道，这其实是一种必然，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not, and I don't mean that, when I say ROI mixing, I don't just mean cutting costs, right?
zh: 不是——我说 ROI 最大化的时候，我不仅仅是指削减成本，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean actually proving some sort of value to the thing that you're doing.
zh: 我是指真正为你正在做的事情证明某种价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not only that, but also kind of opening things up, right?
zh: 不仅如此，还要把局面打开一些，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So if the only thing you have is like two frontier models and their entire stacked ecosystem,
zh: 因为如果你手里只有两个前沿模型以及它们整个堆叠的生态系统，

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a certain cost level where it just makes certain things untenable.
zh: 那就会有一个特定的成本水平，使得某些事情变得难以为继。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't actually expand AI usage into the company if that's the only way you can use AI.
zh: 如果那是你使用 AI 的唯一方式，你实际上无法把 AI 的使用扩展到整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we think about ROI maxing, we first need to think about what are the components of an internal AI deployment.
zh: 所以当我们思考 ROI 最大化时，首先需要思考一个内部 AI 部署由哪些组成部分构成。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not talking about like a, hey, we've built this new AI feature in our app.
zh: 我说的不是那种「嘿，我们在应用里做了一个新 AI 功能」。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean internal to your organization.
zh: 我说的是你组织内部的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's four things.
zh: 一共有四样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the LLM or LLMs.
zh: 有 LLM 或多个 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's that layer.
zh: 有那一层。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's sort of the data connector layer.
zh: 还有所谓的数据连接器层。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is MCP for a lot of people, but in reality it's, you know, CLI or APIs or really just any way that you get data could be reading a file, right, into your agenting system.
zh: 我的意思是，对很多人来说这是 MCP，但实际上它可以是 CLI、API，或者任何你获取数据的方式，比如读一个文件，接入你的智能体系统，对吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the interface.
zh: 有接口这一层。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people kind of forget about this sometimes, but, you know, it started with the chat interface.
zh: 我觉得人们有时候会忘记这一点，但你知道，一切是从聊天界面开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got 2Es, you know, we kind of got a, we got, you know, IDEs with chat.
zh: 我们有了 2Es，你知道，我们有了带聊天的 IDE。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got, you know, kind of a whiplash back from 2Es and, you know, I'm gonna do it on my,
zh: 我们从 2Es 那里经历了剧烈的反弹，你知道，我要在我的——

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to my phone to, oh, now the hot thing is Claude Tag, and I'm going to use, we're just going to interface with agents via Slack.
zh: 打开手机来操作；哦，现在最火的是 Claude Tag，我们就通过 Slack 来和智能体交互吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's another core component, and it is a component that you can break out.
zh: 所以这是另一个核心组成部分，而且是一个你可以拆分出来的组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the last one is sandboxes slash just the environment in which the agent runs.
zh: 然后最后一个是沙箱，也就是智能体运行的环境本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are your four kind of
zh: 所以这就是你的四个大致的

speaker: Unknown
en: Four components, really.
zh: 四个组成部分，真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be ROI maxing means to be maxing every opportunity that you have for choice, to make a choice at one of those layers.
zh: 而做 ROI 最大化，意味着把你拥有的每一个选择机会都最大化，在那些层中的某一层做出选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to necessarily have a unique thing, oh, I've made my bespoke special choice at every one of those layers, but it's really important to be able to make a choice at any given layer that you need at any given time.
zh: 你不一定非要在每一层都做出「哦，我做了专属的独特选择」，但重要的是，能够在任何给定时间，在任何一个你需要的层上做出选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it might be different for different teams or different folks.
zh: 而且这可能因团队不同或人员不同而不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be pretty different across the organization.
zh: 在整个组织内可能会有相当大的差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't totally imagine an entire engineering team just coding via Slack thread.
zh: 我不太能想象一整个工程团队完全通过 Slack 线程来写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might be fun, but I don't totally imagine that.
zh: 那可能挺有趣,但我还是不太能想象那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the entire marketing team might be working entirely in a Slack thread, asking data questions, doing other things like that.
zh: 但整个营销团队可能完全在一个 Slack 线程里工作,问数据问题,做类似这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really important to be able to separate these things.
zh: 所以能够把这些东西区分开是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, right, so I work in TailScale, right?
zh: 而且对,我在 TailScale 工作,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I work on an AI gateway.
zh: 我做的是一个 AI gateway。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, maybe no surprise that I'm here to talk a little bit about why an AI gateway will help you do that, can help you do that.
zh: 我来这里稍微讲一下为什么 AI gateway 能帮你做到这一点、可以帮你做到这一点,可能不足为奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't just mean necessarily using our AI gateway.
zh: 而且我不一定只是指用我们的 AI gateway。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's nice.
zh: 我觉得它挺好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, just any AI gateway is important for this.
zh: 但是,任何 AI gateway 对此都很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our AI gateway is called Aperture.
zh: 我们的 AI gateway 叫做 Aperture。

speaker: Unknown
en: What it does is, right, it's maybe no surprise here, right, but it lets you, it sits in between your agents and that interface of that agent and all of your endpoints as well, both like LLM endpoints and data, kind of MCP endpoints, API endpoints, anything that you have.
zh: 它做的事情是,对,这也许不足为奇,但它让你——它位于你的智能体和那个智能体的接口之间,以及你所有的端点之间,包括 LLM 端点、数据、某种 MCP 端点、API 端点,任何你拥有的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sits in the middle and lets you both control and monitor what's happening.
zh: 它位于中间,让你既能控制也能监控正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That can be from a security perspective.
zh: 那可以是安全角度的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That can be from a cost perspective.
zh: 那可以是成本角度的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That can be from a, which we do a lot, I want to learn about what somebody is doing or what an agent is doing perspective.
zh: 那也可以是——这是我们做很多的——我想了解某个人在做什么或者某个智能体在做什么的角度。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually really cool when you have logs and you can tell your agent to, hey,
zh: 其实当你有日志的时候真的很酷,你可以告诉你的智能体,嘿,

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it ran out.
zh: 也许它跑完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just kind of, oh, it didn't reach an answer.
zh: 它只是,哦,它没有得出答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just kind of spiraled out of control.
zh: 它就是有点失控了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe happens less now.
zh: 也许现在发生得少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely used to happen quite a bit.
zh: 以前肯定发生得挺多的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Happens with maybe cheaper models more often, too.
zh: 在更便宜的模型上可能也发生得更频繁。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're usually not great at stopping themselves, but they are great at analyzing where they went wrong after the fact.
zh: 它们通常不太擅长让自己停下来,但它们很擅长在事后分析自己哪里出错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you have something like an AI gateway, it's really easy to point it back at what you were doing and say, what happened?
zh: 所以当你有像 AI gateway 这样的东西时,让它回看你在做的事情非常容易,然后问,发生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did this not work the way I was expecting it to?
zh: 为什么这没有按我预期的方式运作?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you've used an AI gateway, how many people have an AI gateway, have deployed an AI gateway?
zh: 那么,如果你用过 AI gateway,有多少人有 AI gateway,部署过 AI gateway?

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you've used one before, you're probably used to, OK, so I've put all my keys on this gateway, now I need to go create synthetic keys.
zh: 所以如果你以前用过,你可能习惯了,好,我把所有的密钥都放在了这个 gateway 上,现在我需要去创建合成密钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: For everything that I have.
zh: 为我拥有的所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like, OK, I've traded some keys for a bunch of other keys.
zh: 就像,好,我拿一些密钥换了一堆别的密钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get to do something a little special.
zh: 我们可以做点特别的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Aperture is built on Tailscale.
zh: Aperture 是构建在 Tailscale 上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're not familiar with Tailscale, Tailscale is an identity-based mesh network.
zh: 如果你不熟悉 Tailscale,Tailscale 是一个基于身份的网格网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's built on WireGuard.
zh: 它构建在 WireGuard 之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you get to do with Tailscale is
zh: 你用 Tailscale 能做的事情是——

speaker: Unknown
en: Every connection that is made over a TailNet, so it's a TailScale network, you installed a TailNet agent everywhere that you need.
zh: 每一个在 TailNet 上建立的连接——TailNet 是一个 TailScale 网络——你在需要的每个地方都安装一个 TailNet 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be containers, laptops, GPU servers, doesn't matter.
zh: 可以是容器、笔记本、GPU 服务器,都无所谓。

speaker: Unknown
en: You install it everywhere.
zh: 你在每个地方都安装它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every connection that's now made over that tailnet comes with the identity of the machine or the user on the other side.
